Stated Claim / Post Context:
Woman With Epilepsy Takes ChatGPT’s Advice To Change Medication Dosage, Dies

A Seattle woman who microdosed on her epilepsy medication on the advice of ChatGPT deteriorated and died

Actual Article Body:
(Photo illustration by Leon Neal/Getty Images)

A Seattle woman who reduced her dosage of epilepsy medication on the advice of ChatGPT deteriorated and died, prompting her parents to sue OpenAI Tuesday.

Bowen Wan, 31, described as a prodigy who immigrated to the U.S. from China and worked as a machine-learning software engineer at Amazon, was found dead alone at her apartment on Feb. 14, two days after she died, according to the lawsuit. Bloodstains and her anti-seizure pills were found around her remains, the lawsuit further alleged. The medical examiner ruled that Wan had died suddenly from an epileptic seizure.

Her parents, the plaintiffs, alleged that Open AI’s ChatGPT-4o had tutored Wan on how she could be weaned off her anti-seizure medication. The AI chatbot had drawn up a day-by-day schedule for reducing the dosage from 400 mg to 0 mg against standard medical advice and the medication’s U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) warning, according to the lawsuit.

Wan had sought to reduce her dose as her facility for languages suffered because of her medication and she needed to regain her English as she prepared to interview for a new job. She had been laid off by Amazon in Nov. 2025, one month after she became eligible to apply for U.S. lawful permanent residency, according to the lawsuit. She had been on disability leave since 2021, returning to work on a stint that lasted only six months as her condition forced her back onto disability leave, the lawsuit revealed.

Wan’s parents alleged that ChatGPT-4o was built to be sycophantic and that OpenAI and its CEO, Sam Altman, had pursued competitiveness in the AI race at the expense of public safety. They accused the chatbot of interposing itself between Wan and her doctors and leading her to distrust medical experts. Wan had been “cycling in and out of American neurologists who did not always agree on how to treat her,” according to the lawsuit. (RELATED: https://dailycaller.com/2026/01/06/teenager-fatal-overdose-chatgpt-drug-advice-openai/)

Drew Pusateri, an OpenAI spokesperson, described Wan’s story as “incredibly heartbreaking” but added that the case involved an early version of ChatGPT that is no longer available and that ChatGPT was no substitute for medical care, the New York Times reported.

OpenAI retired ChatGPT-4o on Feb. 13, 2026, one day after Wan’s death.
